profile.campus: Digital Realty Silicon Valley (Santa Clara / Santa Clara County), CA
profile.reading:
This is Digital Realty facility SJC15, at 1201 Comstock Street, Santa Clara, CA 95054. Digital Realty's own property listing for SJC15, fetched this session, lists the building at 24,000 square feet.

Digital Realty Trust (NYSE: DLR, SEC CIK 1297996), headquartered at 2323 Bryan Street, Dallas, Texas, reported 310 data centers worldwide as of December 31, 2025, 221 wholly owned or consolidated and 89 in unconsolidated joint ventures, about 57.6 million rentable square feet across more than 55 metro markets including 118 US facilities, per its FY2025 Form 10-K filed with the SEC. The company operates as a colocation and wholesale landlord rather than running its own compute, distinguishing it from hyperscaler tenants such as AWS, Google, or Meta, also tracked in this registry.

This building sits within Digital Realty's Silicon Valley campus, a dense cluster of buildings across Santa Clara and Santa Clara County that is one of the company's oldest US footprints, reflecting the area's history as a birthplace of the commercial colocation and internet exchange industry. Digital Realty's own Silicon Valley metro page, fetched this session, lists numerous named properties concentrated along Comstock Street, Lafayette Street, and Walsh Avenue, ranging from under 15,000 to nearly 400,000 square feet each. The company does not publish a consolidated IT power rating in megawatts for individual Silicon Valley buildings in the sources reviewed this session.

Digital Realty markets its Silicon Valley properties under its PlatformDIGITAL brand, positioning the metro alongside Northern Virginia, Chicago, Dallas, and New York/New Jersey, all tracked elsewhere in this registry, as core hubs in its global interconnection and colocation platform. The company's FY2025 10-K identifies the United States as its largest single national market by both facility count and rentable square footage.

profile.regional_context: Silicon Valley, anchored by Santa Clara and San Jose, is one of Digital Realty's oldest and densest colocation footprints, reflecting the area's history as the birthplace of the modern internet exchange and enterprise data center industry. PG&E is the principal electric utility serving most of the area, and California's data center growth has drawn scrutiny over grid capacity and water use for cooling in recent years. Silicon Valley also hosts large campuses for Google, Meta, and numerous enterprise and colocation tenants, some tracked elsewhere in this registry, alongside Digital Realty's cluster of smaller, densely packed buildings along Comstock Street, Lafayette Street, and Walsh Avenue in Santa Clara.

reading.body:
Digital Realty's SJC15 facility in Santa Clara contains 24,000 square feet with N+1 cooling redundancy, but the operator publishes no megawatt capacity figure for this building.

The absence of power capacity data for an individual facility within one of Digital Realty's largest US clusters reflects how datacenter operators control disclosure. While cooling redundancy is disclosed, the actual electrical draw remains private. This matters because understanding AI's power footprint requires knowing both the floor space and what it consumes, and published capacity figures remain rare even for named facilities.

SJC15 sits within Digital Realty's broader Silicon Valley campus, which includes historically significant carrier hotels like 365 Main Street in San Francisco. That building's 2007 outage demonstrated the fragility of concentrated hosting infrastructure. The campus operates as a cluster, but individual facility power specifications are not public.

The research status is complete, meaning further investigation would likely not yield the missing megawatt figure. Operators control this information. Without capacity data, SJC15 can be mapped and counted, but not measured against the compute it houses or the grid load it places.
